target: Cuando vivíamos en el campo, teníamos un huerto grande.
english: When we lived in the countryside, we had a big garden.
tip: Both imperfect: vivíamos + teníamos. Describes a habitual past situation, not a single event.

target: Ella se siente sola desde que sus hijos se mudaron.
english: She feels lonely since her children moved away.
tip: English says "has felt lonely since..." – Spanish uses plain present: "se siente sola desde que." If it's still true now, present tense, no perfect needed.

target: Cuanta más información teníamos, más confusa se volvía la situación.
english: The more information we had, the more confusing the situation became.
tip: Comparative correlative: Cuanto más...más = the more...the more.

target: Hay que dejar la masa reposar al menos una hora.
english: You need to let the dough rest for at least an hour.
tip: "Hay que" = literally "there is that..." – Spanish's no-subject must. "Hay que dejar la masa reposar": nobody in particular, everyone in general, has to.

target: Dámelo ahora, por favor; te lo pido como un favor.
english: Give it to me now, please; I'm asking you as a personal favor.
tip: Commands glue pronouns onto the END: "Dámelo" = da+me+lo fused, with an accent added to keep the stress. Compare "te lo pido" – normal pre-verb order returns.

target: Me llamo Ana.
english: My name is Ana.
tip: "Me llamo" = I call myself. The reflexive pronoun "me" refers back to the subject (yo). This is how Spanish states names.

target: Gracias por tu ayuda.
english: Thanks for your help.
tip: "Por" = because of: "Llegué tarde por el tráfico." Expresses the cause behind something.

target: Hace mucho viento hoy.
english: It is very windy today.
tip: Weather uses hacer: 'hace mucho viento' = literally 'it makes much wind.' Viento is a noun, so it takes mucho – 'muy viento' would be 'very wind.'

target: Lo cambié por otro.
english: I exchanged it for another.
tip: "Por" = in exchange for: "Lo compré por diez euros." Por marks what you give to get something.

target: Me cae bien tu amigo.
english: I like your friend.
tip: Gustar for a person can sound romantic. For plain liking, Spanish flips it: "me cae bien" – your friend 'falls well' on me. Safe, attraction-free.

target: Me preocupo por mi familia.
english: I worry about my family.
tip: "Por" = about / concerning: "Preguntó por ti." Por when asking or worrying about someone.

target: Ojalá haga buen tiempo mañana.
english: I hope the weather is good tomorrow.
tip: "Ojalá" descends from Arabic 'law sha Allah' (if God willed) – it expresses a wish, not a fact, so it always takes subjunctive: ojalá "haga" buen tiempo.

target: Cuando llegues al hotel, avísame.
english: When you arrive at the hotel, let me know.
tip: "Cuando" + future action uses subjunctive: "cuando llegues" (not "cuando llegas").

target: Me despierto temprano todos los días.
english: I wake up early every day.
tip: Spanish splits waking in two: despertar is waking someone else up. To wake up on your own, you turn the verb back on yourself – me despierto, 'I wake myself.'

target: Necesito un hotel que tenga estacionamiento.
english: I need a hotel that has parking.
tip: Subjunctive in relative clauses: "que tenga" because the hotel is hypothetical/unknown. If the hotel were known, you'd use indicative.

target: Sin que nadie se dé cuenta, salimos.
english: Without anyone noticing, we left.
tip: Don't reach for 'realizar' – that means to carry out a plan. To notice/realize is darse cuenta, literally 'give yourself account': here, "se dé cuenta".

target: Mi madre quiere que la llame más.
english: My mother wants me to call her more.
tip: Querer que + subjunctive: wanting someone else to do something. "Quiero que vengas" (I want you to come). Different subjects → subjunctive.

target: Me levanto a las siete de la mañana.
english: I get up at seven in the morning.
tip: Clock times run plural – a las siete, roughly 'at the sevens' – with one exception: 1:00 is a la una, singular, because there's only one of it.

target: Me caí en la calle y me hice daño.
english: I fell in the street and hurt myself.
tip: "Caerse" = to fall down (accidentally). Reflexive adds accidental nuance: "Me caí" = I fell (it happened to me).

target: Mi hermano es alto, pero hoy está enfermo y está en cama.
english: My brother is tall, but today he is sick and is in bed.
tip: Same brother, two verbs: "es alto" – height is who he is; "está enfermo" – sickness is just today's condition. Ser for identity, estar for state.

target: Me queda grande esta camiseta.
english: This t-shirt is too big for me.
tip: "Quedar" for fit/appearance: "Te queda bien" = It looks good on you / It fits you well. Uses indirect object like gustar.

target: Busco un hotel que tenga piscina.
english: I'm looking for a hotel that has a pool.
tip: Subjunctive in adjective clauses: when describing something unknown or that might not exist. "Busco alguien que hable francés."

target: A veces me quedo dormido en el sofá.
english: Sometimes I fall asleep on the sofa.
tip: "Quedarse dormido" = to fall asleep (accidentally). "Quedarse" + adjective means "to end up/become": quedarse solo, quedarse callado.

target: Busco a alguien que sepa hablar tres idiomas.
english: I'm looking for someone who can speak three languages.
tip: Sepa, not sabe: this alguien may not even exist – you're describing a wish, not a found person. Once found, back to indicative: conozco a alguien que sabe.

target: Mientras caminábamos por la playa, encontramos unas conchas.
english: While we were walking on the beach, we found some shells.
tip: Two pasts, one scene: "caminábamos" (imperfect) describes the ongoing background action; "encontramos" (preterite) is the completed event that happened during it.

target: Por mucho que lo intente, no consigo entenderlo.
english: No matter how much I try, I can't manage to understand it.
tip: "Por mucho que" + subjunctive – no matter how much.

target: Es mejor que reserves con anticipación para conseguir buen precio.
english: It's better that you book in advance to get a good price.
tip: Es mejor que bends the next verb into subjunctive – reserves, not reservas – because booking early is a recommendation about what should happen, not a report of what did.

target: El nuevo proyecto es coser y cantar si nos organizamos bien.
english: The new project is a piece of cake if we organize well.
tip: Coser y cantar is literally 'to sew and sing' – work so effortless you can carry a tune while doing it. Same move as 'piece of cake': measure ease by a mindless pleasure.

target: ¿Cómo te llamas?
english: What's your name?
tip: Spanish asks how you call yourself: "te llamas" is reflexive llamarse. "¿Cómo te llamas?" is literally 'How do you call yourself?' – no word for 'name' in sight.

target: Estoy haciéndolo ahora.
english: I'm doing it now.
tip: In 'haciéndolo', the pronoun lo attaches to the end of the gerund.
